gen-gf-revalia-archivo: Archivo brings a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, a plain sans with an editorial streak. Revalia sits above it with a loose, relaxed stride and a lowercase g that leaves its lower curve open.
gen-gf-revalia-fs-asap: Open arcs on the c and a body height close to the capitals make Asap easy to settle into. Revalia earns its place big and short, where its widely spaced letters can swagger.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-epilogue: Epilogue is a plain sans with a wire-like skeleton, tall lowercase and stubby ascender tips. And Early GameBoy stretches out its tracking above it, adding a mild taper at the bends that the body's heavy bowls never attempt.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-general-sans: A towering lowercase and widely separated letters give Eight Bit Dragon its adventurous stride, with only a slight pinch where curves meet stems. General Sans follows with smooth, unpinched bends, and that quiet consistency is what holds the pair together.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-manrope: Fast and pushy, Ethnocentric sets short ascenders over big bowls and shoves its letters apart with positive tracking. Manrope answers with bright open curves and a pen line that never wavers.
gen-dafont-galaxy-satoshi: Satoshi stands tall with a soaring x-height, a wide-open e that never looks squeezed, and every stroke cut to one width. Galaxy's loose, spacious letterfit gives the pair its cosmic feel.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-work-sans: Bowls that nearly seal shut and a leisurely, wobbly pace make Jelly Crazies instantly playful, with no calligraphic thinning at all. Work Sans sits beside it with open c tips and a high mean line, giving the wobble somewhere to rest.
gen-dafont-joystix-fs-public-sans: Joystix is arcade-bold, widely tracked, with stems barely heavier than the arms joining them. Public Sans brings a hefty lowercase and broad open counters on c and s, so long paragraphs would read steadily and with trust.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-switzer: Neuropolitical pulls words apart letter by letter, its neon-tube forms glowing at one steady line thickness. But Switzer is the one built for sustained reading, with wire-like letters, a tall waist line and c tips that never creep together.
gen-dafont-impact-label-general-sans: General Sans reads smoothly, its pressure steady from first letter to last and its x-height filling the line. Impact Label hits hard with isolated, heavy letters, while the sans simply carries the eye along.
